changes: Auth-store account changes synchronously clear group list/history/error/loading and shared plaintext drafts. Pending account work is invalidated by an account epoch, including logout/re-login to the same account. Existing sidebar read-affinity guards are retained.

Group history/search and incoming decryption capture current membership/key epoch and group lifetime. Late replies after account change, membership removal or rekey are discarded. Optional transport guards also prevent stale requests from being retried after token refresh.

History loads merge instead of replacing live state. Per-message mutation clocks prevent delayed history/decryption from resurrecting a deletion or erasing a newer edit/arrival. Pending duplicate create decryptions are suppressed. A membership removal invalidates old group lifetimes.

Send/edit check group scope and device before HTTP and after asynchronous encryption/cache stages. Confirmed plaintext is not added under a changed account/group. Cache writes accept a guard and recheck after IndexedDB opening. Group batch decryption discards stale cached/decrypted plaintext and passes the same guard to cache writes.
Text editing retains original encrypted attachment keys in the payload and local message. A local cache-write failure after a confirmed send/edit no longer reports the committed operation as failed.

Group composer now uses the existing memory-only, account/conversation-keyed draft store and send tickets. Navigation restores each group's draft; a pending response cannot clear newer typing or a failed send's draft. Group reply/edit context fields are scoped with the draft.

Synchronous account cleanup exposed an existing unstable empty-array selector in GroupDMChat; replaced it with a stable empty message list to prevent a maximum-update-depth failure after logout/account switch.
verification: 6 focused files / 116 tests passed, covering store races, composer drafts, group decryption, real fake-indexeddb cache semantics and existing Signal/DM encryption regressions.
Full client regression: 221 files / 2076 tests passed in 45.26s. Existing jsdom navigation warnings were not suppressed. Correct tsc -b and targeted ESLint passed before this run.

New cases include account/member/rekey/device changes during encryption, late history, live edit/delete merge, pending decryption vs deletion, stale cache read/write, attachment-key preservation, cache failure after commit, draft navigation, newer typing during send and failed-send draft retention.
Initial component regression caught the unstable empty-array selector during account cleanup; fixed the actual selector rather than bypassing the account-change assertion.

Inspection confirms apiClient checks isCurrent before the initial request, after proactive token refresh and after a 401 refresh before retry. No server schema or production data changed in this follow-up.
Local Vite production web build succeeded (1645 modules). Existing config-loader, large-chunk and ineffective-dynamic-import warnings remain; no warning suppression or publication occurred.
remaining: Group edited-message cache versioning was subsequently implemented (p4-group-cache-versions-2026-10-24.json). Real two-client edited-message acceptance remains pending; unverifiable edited legacy caches are retained but not displayed as the latest version.

Low-level Signal ratchet/session writes during account switch are not proven isolated by these plaintext/UI guards. Broader cryptographic lifecycle cancellation and actual multi-device tests remain required; no end-to-end account isolation acceptance is claimed.
Membership/profile mutation responses and group-call component lifetime still need broader stale-response hardening outside the covered load/send/edit paths.

Pre-edit draft backup/restore was subsequently implemented (p4-group-edit-drafts-2026-10-24.json). Real navigation/keyboard and recovery acceptance still remains; group drafts do not close all composer acceptance.
Search still has a 100-page bound/partial-failure behavior; complete-search signaling and real two-client/browser/Windows acceptance remain open. Browser space is still handed to the user.
